summary: DAAD EPOS funds professionals from developing countries to take selected development-related master's (and some PhD) courses in Germany. It pays a monthly stipend (EUR 992 for master's students; higher for doctoral candidates), health insurance and a travel allowance. Winners are graduates with at least two years of relevant work, good grades, and a clear plan to use the degree back home.
lookfor: At least two years of relevant professional experience after your bachelor's
Above-average degree results (roughly the top third of your class)
Clear link between your job, the course, and development impact in your home country
Motivation letter that explains your choice and priority of courses
Employer support, ideally with a promise to re-employ you after study
cycle: You apply directly to the course, not to DAAD. For 2027/28 most course deadlines fell between about June and October 2026, so many have passed; check the official deadline list for any still open. Courses shortlist and nominate candidates, then DAAD asks nominees to upload a full application to the DAAD Portal and makes final decisions. The list for the next round (2028/29) usually appears mid-2027.

eligibility.q: Are you a national of a country on the DAAD EPOS (DAC) eligible-country list?
eligibility.no: EPOS is only for developing and emerging countries. Try Erasmus Mundus or university scholarships instead.

eligibility.q: Will you have at least two years of relevant full-time professional work after your bachelor's by the course deadline?
eligibility.no: Keep working and apply next round. Some courses do not count internships or volunteering — ask the course whether NYSC counts before relying on it.

eligibility.q: Is your degree no more than about six years old?
eligibility.no: DAAD says degrees should normally not be older than six years. Ask the course coordinator whether an exception is possible before applying.

eligibility.q: Were your results above average (upper third)?
eligibility.no: Choose courses where your work experience is especially relevant, and consider other awards with lower grade weight.

eligibility.q: Have you lived in Germany for less than 15 months at the deadline?
eligibility.no: You cannot be considered. Look at other DAAD programmes.

eligibility.q: Is a course on the EPOS list in your field still open for applications?
eligibility.no: Prepare now for the next round, which usually publishes its course list around mid-year.

steps.title: Pick up to three EPOS courses that match your job
steps.why: You can apply to at most three courses in priority order, and each course selects people whose work fits its focus.
do: Open the DAAD EPOS deadline list and the current EPOS brochure linked from the DAAD EPOS page.
Filter by your field (e.g. water, energy, agriculture, public health, economics).
For each course, open its own website: note deadline, language, required degree, and how to apply (email, portal or uni-assist).
Choose up to three courses and rank them.
tips: Your first choice should be the one that fits your current job best; selectors check this link.
avoid: Applying to courses whose deadline has already passed or that need German if you have none.
check: I have up to three ranked courses with live deadlines.

steps.title: Check you meet every rule
steps.why: Incomplete or ineligible applications are not considered.
do: Read the EPOS entry in the DAAD scholarship database.
Count your relevant work months after your bachelor's; you need 24+.
Check your degree date (normally within six years) and your class of degree.
Check your country on the eligible-country list.
tips: Write your work history as dates and hours now — you will reuse it in the CV and employer letters.
avoid: Counting internships or student jobs without checking the course rules.
check: I meet the experience, degree-age and country rules.

steps.title: Build your timeline and download the forms
steps.why: Employer letters, certified copies and English tests all take weeks.
do: Write each course deadline in your calendar, with your own deadline one week earlier.
Download the DAAD checklist and the DAAD application form ('Application for a research/study scholarship') from the course or DAAD page.
Check each course's own extra requirements (some use uni-assist or their own portal).
Make a folder per course for files.
tips: Some courses want everything as one PDF in a set order — follow it exactly.
check: I have the current forms and every course's submission method.

steps.title: Get your employer letter and employment certificates
steps.why: Proof of two years' relevant work is required, and employer backing strengthens your case.
do: Ask HR for employment certificates showing your job title, start and end dates and full-time status.
Ask your manager for a letter on official letterhead, signed and stamped, that supports your study leave.
If possible, include a statement that you will be re-employed after study.
Scan everything in colour as PDF.
tips: Give your manager a short draft of the points to cover; they will sign faster.
check: My letters cover 24+ months and are signed and stamped.

steps.title: Get certified degree certificate and transcripts
steps.why: DAAD asks for certified copies plus an explanation of the grading system.
do: Request official transcripts from your university's Exams and Records office.
Get certified copies of certificate and transcripts as the course instructs.
Get a document explaining your grading system (often on the transcript back, or a letter from the registry).
Add certified English or German translations if originals are in another language.
tips: Ask the registry for your class position or a statement of ranking if it shows you are in the upper third.
avoid: Uploading uncertified photocopies when certified copies are asked for.
check: I have certified, readable copies plus grading explanation.

steps.title: Prove your language level
steps.why: Applications without accepted language proof are incomplete.
do: Check each course's English requirement (IELTS or TOEFL; institutional TOEFL is not accepted by DAAD).
Book the test early enough for results before the deadline.
For German-taught courses, you need at least B1 German at application and a higher exam before study.
tips: Some courses accept English-medium degree proof — ask the course coordinator in writing.
check: My language proof meets every course's requirement.

steps.title: Write your Europass CV
steps.why: Your CV shows the relevance of your work to development.
do: Create a CV in reverse chronological order (DAAD recommends the Europass template).
For each job, write 2–3 lines on responsibilities and results, with dates.
Add training, projects, publications and languages.
Sign and date it if the course asks.
tips: Use numbers: budgets handled, people served, projects led.
check: My CV is complete, dated and in reverse order.

steps.title: Write your motivation letter
steps.why: It is the main place selectors judge your commitment and development impact.
do: Paragraph 1: the development problem you work on, with one example from your job.
Paragraph 2: your experience so far and what you achieved.
Paragraph 3: why these courses and why in this priority order; name modules.
Paragraph 4: what you will do after returning, and how your employer or community benefits.
Keep to the limit; save as PDF and sign if required.
tips: DAAD explicitly asks you to explain your course choice and priority if you apply to more than one.
avoid: A generic letter about Germany's beauty.
check: The letter explains my course ranking and my return plan.

steps.prompt: Detailed reasons for applying, including your choice and prioritisation of courses.
steps.limit: Commonly a maximum of two pages — check each course's current guidance.

steps.title: Fill the DAAD application form
steps.why: The form is part of the required set and is checked again at DAAD stage.
do: Fill personal details, education, work history and the courses you apply to.
Make dates match your CV and employer letters exactly.
Sign and date the form and the checklist.
Save as PDF.
tips: Watch tutorials that show the form section by section (see videos).
check: The form is complete, signed and consistent.

steps.title: Arrange reference letters
steps.why: Courses usually want academic and professional referees; letters may need to come directly from them.
do: Check each course's number and type of references.
Ask a former lecturer and your supervisor at work.
Send them your CV, the course link and key points to mention.
Ask how the course wants letters sent (often direct by email from the referee) and share the deadline.
tips: Professional referees should mention your development work and its impact.
avoid: Collecting sealed letters when the course wants them emailed directly.
check: Each referee knows the method and deadline.

steps.title: Assemble and submit to each course
do: Order your documents exactly as the checklist says.
Merge into one PDF if the course asks; check file size.
Submit by the course's method (email, portal or uni-assist).
Save the confirmation email or screenshot.
tips: Also apply for regular admission if the course says this is separate.
avoid: Sending to DAAD instead of the course.
check: I have a submission confirmation for each course.

steps.title: Prepare for the course interview
steps.why: Many EPOS courses interview shortlisted applicants before nominating them to DAAD.
do: Watch your email, including spam.
Prepare short answers: your job, the problem you tackle, why this course, your return plan.
Test your connection and set up a quiet room.
tips: Bring concrete numbers from your job.
check: I can explain my development plan in two minutes.

steps.title: Upload to the DAAD Portal if nominated
steps.why: Nomination is not the final award; DAAD checks your documents and decides.
do: When DAAD emails you, register on the DAAD Portal.
Upload the full application set requested.
Meet the DAAD upload deadline in the email.
tips: Keep all PDFs from your course application ready to reuse.
check: My DAAD Portal application shows as submitted.

steps.title: Accept the award and plan your visa
steps.why: German visa appointments in many African countries book up far ahead.
do: Accept the scholarship and course admission in writing.
Book a German embassy or consulate visa appointment as soon as you have your award letter.
Arrange study leave with your employer.
If unsuccessful, ask for feedback and prepare for the next course list mid-2027.
tips: Some courses start with a German language course before the semester.
avoid: Resigning before your visa is issued.
check: I have my award letter and a visa appointment.

faq.q: Do I apply to DAAD directly?
faq.a: No. You apply to the course; the course nominates candidates and DAAD then asks nominees to upload to the DAAD Portal.

faq.q: How many courses can I apply to?
faq.a: Up to three, in priority order, explained in your motivation letter.

faq.q: Does NYSC count as work experience?
faq.a: Not confirmed. Ask each course coordinator in writing before relying on it.
EUR 992 a month for master's students, plus insurance and travel allowance; possible rent and family allowances.

faq.q: The deadline for my course has passed. What now?
faq.a: Prepare for the next round; course lists usually appear around mid-year.
